title: Verifying full quantum network nonlocality in arbitrary configurations by nonlinear Bell-like inequalities
authors: Shuyuan Yang, Jinchuan Hou, Kan He, Mingxing Luo
abstract: Full quantum network nonlocality (FQNN) describes a scenario where all sources in a network are nonlocal. Existing criteria of FQNN can only be verified in star networks by violating a single Bell-like inequality. Here we propose a method that certifies FQNN in general quantum networks using only a single Bell-like inequality. We show that the topological obstacle to one-shot detection can be overcome by expanding the original network with a carefully chosen number of auxiliary local sources and parties. The correlations of the enlarged network are then tested with a single inequality; a violation implies that all original sources must be nonlocal. Our approach provides an efficient, experimentally friendly way to verify FQNN in any network topology.
summary: This paper introduces a novel method to verify Full Quantum Network Nonlocality (FQNN) across any network topology using just one nonlinear Bell-like inequality. The technique involves augmenting the original network with auxiliary local sources and testing the resulting structure against a derived inequality. A violation of this single test proves that all original quantum sources exhibit genuine nonlocality.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a method to verify Full Quantum Network Nonlocality (FQNN) in quantum networks with arbitrary topologies.
main_result: The authors propose an efficient technique that certifies FQNN using only a single nonlinear Bell-like inequality, overcoming limitations of previous topology-specific tests.
method: They enlarge the original network by adding carefully chosen auxiliary local sources and parties. The resulting augmented network is then tested with a single derived $l$-QNL inequality.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum networks distributing entangled states among spatially separated parties ($S_1, S_2, \dots$). Specific examples analyzed include triangular, chain, and cyclic network topologies ($\Xi(n, m)$).
key_observables: Violation of the derived nonlinear Bell-like inequality (e.g., $|	ext{Inew}|_1/4 + |	ext{Jnew}|_1/4 > 	ext{Bound}$), which implies that all original sources must be nonlocal.
important_parameters: The maximum independent number ($h$) and the topological parameters defining the network structure are crucial for constructing the inequality.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that violating the derived inequality provides a conclusive proof of FQNN, and concrete calculations sometimes assume sources are in Werner states.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the concept using triangular networks (showing augmentation), chain networks, and cyclic networks, detailing how auxiliary local sources expand the original structure for testing.
paper_structure: The paper develops a general inequality based on network topology parameters ($h$) and then applies this method to specific, complex topologies like $\Xi(3, 3)$, chain networks ($\Xi(n, n-1)$), and cyclic networks ($\Xi(n, n)$) through augmentation.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general tool for certifying fundamental quantum properties (nonlocality) in complex, realistic network architectures, which is highly relevant to quantum communication protocols.
